utterances.text: And I will tell you, I submit to you that that is the designation that I have as listed there as the house of Nada Stabac as well as the house of Boris Kupovic which is very nearby?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go to the next slide. Sir, I'm not going to go through these seriatim but I just ask you to you take a look at these. Just take a moment. I realize this is not something that you've seen before, but these are the locations, and I have interposed government and military infrastructure items over it that have previously been received in evidence. And as can you see from the various numbers, the As are ARSK troops bases and barracks; the B numbers are command and control and power; C numbers are anti-aircraft units; the D numbers are military industry and depots; and the E numbers are transportation infrastructure.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just take a moment and just take a look at them and try to familiarize yourself with it. Now, looking at this, sir, is it your testimony that looking at all of these various and -- that no public buildings were hit during the shelling of Knin on the 4th and 5th? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I said as long as I know, I saw no hit to public buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let us turn to the -- and let me just look at the slides here, which is B1, which is the ARSK main headquarters; B2, which is the ARSK -- it's part of the Defence ministry; B3, ARSK office accommodation, and even before this, another item, which is a commander-in-chief residence. If we can go to the next -- oh, that's good. I can see that better. If we can go to the next slide. Sir, this is a blow-up of your area of your residence you designated in the map as A. I have put the address of L. Marunda 32 at its proper location to the right of A as well as Boris' house, which is also to the right of A. Now, you're familiar with this location, are you not, sir?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the area there that's B1, which is the headquarters of the army of the Republic of Serb Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I think it was that building during the night I could hear a diesel motor going. I don't know, but I -- from my place I could hear diesel going through the night for --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this building, I mean, obviously it's approximately less than -- at least part of that facility is less than 50 metres from your residence. In the morning of the 5th, did you hear shells being -- hitting the RSK headquarters?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You did not?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No. Let me tell you that -- the shelling, I was keeping my head down, so I couldn't see, let's say, where -- that I heard from later on when you hear these shelling coming, it's a sound, and when you hear it, you can sit there, but if you don't hear it, you should go down because then the shelling will coming for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me -- given your location and you were at -- in your residence on the 4th when the shelling took place; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you were in your residence the entire day of the 4th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And is it your testimony that you were unaware of B1, the ARSK headquarters, being hit?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Have I said that I saw that this was hit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, I'm asking you, sir, were you aware that it was either through sound or hearing or in some other fashion?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I might have just one moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you noted -- I'm sorry. You noted during the correspondence of your testimony or just now, be that as it may, that you heard a diesel engine running. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And what did you think that that was supplying power to? Did you have any idea?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I mean, was it trucks or was it equipment --

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No, no, no trucks. It could be for electricity, I would -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you aware, sir, that during this period of time the -- if we look just a little further north that the railway facility, for instance, around E 8 was hit by -- by -- during the artillery attack?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I couldn't see anything there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, did you hear it?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes, but if you hear and you're sitting inside here, for example, and you hear the shelling outside you can't see where it goes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How about these other RSK facilities which were approximately 150 to 200 metres from you, and I'm talking about B2 and B3 over to the left? Did you hear -- hear, now, did you hear those buildings being hit by artillery fire?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No. I can't say I hear any building got hit. I thought later on, but it's impossible to sit inside and say, Oh, he hit -- they hit this house or something. I can't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, sir, let me understand you well. When you said in your statement that -- and I go back to your statement, P721, paragraph 6, you say as far as you could see no public buildings were hit. You're just saying you didn't see them being hit. You're not saying that they weren't hit?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: What I'm writing there is what happened later on when I went outside and walking around. So this is not from the 4th or the 5th. It must be later on when I was outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let me show you -- okay. Let me show you, just before we get to that, D389.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would tender 1D43 0001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, but first, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: If the Prosecution could just have a day or two to review the locations and verify the accuracy compared to the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well, way of two might be a bit -- you presented very unclear maps. Therefore, I think -- and since the witness will leave us today most likely ...

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I can review it in the break, Your Honour, and get back to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you, please, will do that, and then we'll see how far you come.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Registrar, that would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become Exhibit number D718 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And now just for my information, Mr. Kehoe, that's the blown-up version or the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Just the blown-up version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just the blown-up version. That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The other one being an introduction rather than ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's right, sir. I just tried to put it in perspective and then blow it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. -- let me just see. D719, we'll take a decision on that once we have heard from the Prosecution after the break. Of course, you are missing the agenda, but we have this agenda on other maps that are -- other photographs which are already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I take it that the numbering is fully consistent with what we have seen earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It is consistent with the addition -- I will tell you, I put in the addition of the items that the witness put in, which is the school, which had the soldiers in it, which had not been designated the prior to that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that would be, Judge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the school would be, anyhow, on the Prosecution's map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's on the Prosecution map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the locations where people were living, I think, as a matter of fact do not appear, the -- Boris' house, and these are new, as well, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's correct, Judge. Those two we put on with using the witness's address and, also, with Boris's address. We made that more accurate than the rather global A point that the witness put in, which he did some 13 years --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you take the witness back for one second to these houses so as to ask him to identify whether they're located -- his own apartment being in the centre of the circles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that is what he already testified, but let's just make that for once and forever sure, perhaps the blown-up version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The blown-up version, Judge. This is the blown-up version, Your Honour, the green give -- taken from the witness's address, which he puts on page 1 of his statement in 1995, P721. He addresses L. Marunda 32 in Knin, and the -- checking the address logs, that's in fact the address, and the individual he identified as Boris is living in the -- the green square just to the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's at least what we now have to ask the witness. Could you confirm that the small green feature just in the middle of the concentric circles, is that the apartment building in which you lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It seems so, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the green rectangular feature just left of that on the radius, 50 metres line, is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the building where the person you called Boris was living.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have identified that. I think that would for the moment do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: May I just clarify on the record, Judge. This is a 4-page document. If we can go to prior page, certainly, we're putting all four pages in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No further questions were put to the witness in respect of these apart from whether this was the -- and that's for the Prosecution to verify whether the markings are the same as on the original marked aerial photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said four pages?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yeah. The other two pages were, again -- if we could go to page 1 and page 2 just to put Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, that's the whole with the agenda?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour. It wasn't really an agenda. It was just this -- these are the items, and the next page are the ones -- we took out the ones that were non-shelling-related per Mr. Widen's testimony, if we can go to the next line, because he does discuss things that are not shelling-related which aren't pertinent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. For the first three, of course, it's important that he -- that the Prosecution verifies whether the markings which have been reproduced on this map in a slightly different way, whether these are the same markings as we find on the map marked by the witness, and now, therefore, it's not only the blown-up version but all four pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: All four, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will, then, decide on that. Mr. Registrar, D719 would then be all four pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that it's actually 718, D718, four pages. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We were talking about D389. If we could bring that back on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Widen, this is an ARSK intelligence report from the morning of the 4th of August, 1995, and if I could turn your attention basically to the centre of this page. It says: "Knin was attacked ..." If you could focus your attention on that.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And it notes that this is coming from the ARSK themselves, that Knin was attacked from Livanjsko Polje from several directions by the time this information was drafted, between 200 and 300 rounds of different calibres impacted on the town. "The first strike was carried out on the building SVK General Staff." Now, sir, that's the building that is -- begins approximately 40 metres from your residence, which suffered great material damage with a fleet of vehicles almost completely destroyed. Did you see the parking lot at any point behind the ARSK headquarters with the vehicles destroyed in that parking lot that was very near your home?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No, I didn't because it's close to my home, but you have a lot of trees, so you can't look into it from my place. It was a lot of trees there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Later, the -- it continues on: "Later, the fire was transferred on military barracks 1300 Kapalara." Are you familiar with shells landing either on the barracks that were in town or the barracks that were outside of town, the northern barracks?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The next is the Tvik factory. Do you know where the Tvik factory is in town, sir?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You don't know where that is?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you see during this time big plumes of black smoke coming out of a factory in the centre of town?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I didn't think about that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And obviously, you know, we talked about the railway intersection, that you didn't see any shelling at the railway intersection. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Let's say from my -- when you're driving a car or walking, you can't see -- I mean, it is a big area, and if it was an impact there, I can't say. But I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, again, if we can clarify it, you're not saying it didn't happen; you just didn't go inside those facilities to see if they had in fact been shelled?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Let's say we were not allowed to go wherever we want to go at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you another item, which is a -- P214, which is a statement by Mr. Elleby. Now, did you talk to Mr. Elleby, you know, during this entire time when you were working together at CIVPOL?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I met him, let's say, two years later in Copenhagen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: When you were still back at Sector South, at the headquarters in Sector South when you folks were all together, did you discuss matters with Mr. Elleby and the other CIVPOL members?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Of course we did, but I can't remember some special thing, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let me go -- this is a -- Mr. Elleby's statement on 17 September 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page, and the second paragraph, if we can just blow that up second paragraph a bit. It notes: "After 8 August 1995, he" - being Mr. Elleby - "noticed the most destruction had occurred in the areas around the Serb military barracks and the government buildings. Some areas in Knin seemed being nearly unharmed by the shelling. F," - I think, for example - "the area near the Knin hospital was nearly unharmed." Did you have discussions with Mr. Elleby where he shared these types of observations with you?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the Prosecution during the course of their -- the briefing of you showed you P228, which is a UN assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can bring that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: By the way, Mr. Widen, do you have any reason to question the conclusions by Mr. Elleby?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we turn our attention to this document, this is a document that you said -- that you had -- you told the Prosecution that you had not seen until they showed it to you. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And in the second paragraph -- by the way, are you familiar with the individual who wrote this?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I know Thor Hansen. I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, this one is Steinar Hagvag.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: He is also a Norwegian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And he notes in the second paragraph: "We cover the whole township, observed several impacts of shells and rockets around the Tvik factory, the military headquarters, the general direction of the northern barracks, shells coming from north-east and government house, the Knin radio/TV building, and the hillside below Knin." Now, did you notice shelling damage on any of these locations as Mr. Hagvag writes here?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss this with him?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No. Let's say I was not that many days in, and I was looking into my own area and saw some houses who blown up there, and this is -- perhaps they have order from higher up to make this observation, but not for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I just wanted to point out that the question was, Did you note shelling on any of these locations that Mr. Hagvag writes here. The report says --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. This is cross-examination. I'm asking him about these locations.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Well, the report says that Mr. Hagvag observed several impacts of shells around the certain locations, and I'm -- just think that's not precisely the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Locations have, then, to be understood as areas around the specifically mentioned objects, that is the Tvik factory, milicija headquarters, and it goes even without saying if we're talking about the general direction of north barracks, that already refers to general directions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, did you see shelling around these particular locations?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No. I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So when you told that the Prosecution, "I have never seen this report before, and I" -- this is in paragraph 27 of P722: "I have never seen this report before, and I did not participate in this assessment. I cannot recall anyone mentioning this assessment or its findings. In reviewing the assessment, I note that there is no mention of impacts directly on any of the facilities referenced but only observations of shell impacts around these areas, which is consistent with my recollection." Now, I just asked you whether or not if you heard or you observed shelling around those locations and you said no. So is what the Prosecute -- what was it written in this statement incorrect?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I'm not following you right now. I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, the Prosecution typed -- wrote this, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: If you say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, I'm asking you, sir.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: What is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's your statement. It's your statement in 2008.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. That I have here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And your testimony before this Chamber is that you did not observe any shelling around the Tvik factory, the military headquarters, the northern barracks, the government house, the Knin radio or TV station. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. What I did was to mark on this map those places where I saw shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you did not observe -- excuse me. So when you told the Prosecution, sir, that that -- in paragraph 27 that this report is consistent with your observations, it's really not consistent with your observations, is it, because you said that you didn't see shelling around the Tvik factory, the military headquarters, the northern barracks, government house, the Knin radio station; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I will say -- I can't say that I saw any shelling there, and that is it because I brought -- perhaps not visit these areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that's because, as you noted in your paragraph 38 of 722, if you look at paragraph 38: "I never patrolled or visited east side of Knin, including south-east to north-east." Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that Mr. Hjertnes was a Norwegian, and I think you also mentioned Steinar. I mean, you knew Mr. Steinar Hjertnes, did you not, who was the Senior Military Observer?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I can't remember the name now, but Steinar, he was not in Knin when the Storm started.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But you know that he was the senior UNMO?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you P64. Have you ever seen this document before? This is a provisional assessment that was dated 18 August 1995 and signed by the Senior Military Observer, Sector South, Mr. Hjertnes.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No, I haven't seen this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In paragraph 2, it notes that in general, shelling was concentrated against military objectives. The damage caused by shelling to civilian establishments is concentrated to the close vicinity of military objectives. Only a few, three or five impacts is observed in other urban areas." When you were in the Sector South headquarters, Mr. Widen, did you discuss -- or was these conclusions discussed in and among the various personnel in UN Sector South?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No, not what I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the -- you yourself never did a formal shelling assessment, did you?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You never were assigned to go out and do a formal shelling assessment?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No, no. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You never wrote a report on it, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let me -- I'm sorry, I'm just -- I might take a break there. I'm just waiting for the translation to catch up, so ...

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So just bear with me a second. Now, you mentioned several items in your statement, and talking specifically about -- in paragraph 24, you noted that the -- this is of your 2008 statement, 722, P722. In the last sentence, you said you would like to clarify that "the stolen UN pick-up trucks I saw with heavy machine-guns or rocket launchers were not located at the school but were just driving around Knin." Now, turning your attention back to your 1995 statement, and I will try to piece these items together, and we're talking about 721, and we're talking about page 8 of your -- excuse me. It should be paragraph 8, I believe. Paragraph 8. That would be page 4. You noted in -- towards the bottom of that page, and can you see that sentence beginning: "During that assault in the Knin ..."? That's in the bottom section of that paragraph. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: What do you mean? How --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The sentence says, "During the assault on Knin, I heard noises indicative of ..." Do you see that sentence?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It says, "During the assault on Knin, I heard noises indicative of missiles being launched and suggestion that there may have been some attempt to defend Knin."

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you wrote this in December of 1995?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: So then it must be true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And what you believed at the time was that the missiles that you heard were outgoing missiles being fired by the Serbs. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: That was I was thinking here when I wrote this, but I'm not an expert on this, so I can't ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, sir, that you're an expert, but when you were sitting in your house on the 4th of August and you heard outgoing missiles, you concluded that the outgoing missiles were coming from the Serbs, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: That -- I can't remember it now, but when I read it I can see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yeah, so that was your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, sir, let me -- by the way, sir, in addition to -- and this outgoing fire by the Serbs, you heard that on the 4th of August?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: If it's written here, I did, but I can't remember that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Could the diesel engine that you have -- that you heard, could it have been operating a mobile rocket launcher?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you know that the -- if the rocket launchers you observed were the missiles that you heard being fired out?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I can't say that, either, because what I saw was on the trucks, and I think they were ready to fire from the trucks. I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well -- and they were travelling around.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So you don't know exactly where they fired from?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: After the Serbs withdrew on the 4th, do you know of the Serbs firing back into the Croats -- back into Knin on the Croats? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you know about any fire coming from Serb-held area onto -- excuse me, on Serb-held area onto the HV on the 5th?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, the shelling damage that you observed -- let me withdrew that for a second. If in fact the Serbs were firing at various locations on the 4th as you concluded from your statement, and if there was firing by the Serbs on the Croats into Knin on the 5th, the damage you observed, you don't know who fired the weaponry that caused that damage, do you?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Of course, I can't say that because I was sitting, hiding myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, sir. I'd be there too. Believe me, I don't think there's a person in this room who wouldn't be with you. Now, if we can go back, if we can, to D718, and if I can go to the fourth slide on D718. Now, sir, by the time the 5th of August rolled around, you were at Boris' house, were you not?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I came there around 1800.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: On what --

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: On -- the afternoon, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. And when you heard this kicking in of doors and going into various locations with shooting, was that on the 4th or the 5th? That was on the 5th?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: That was on the 5th around 1500.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And where were you? You were in Boris's?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No, I was in my apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, when you were in your apartment and you heard this, this is -- and taking this location, that would put you approximately 40 metres away from the ARSK headquarters, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah, if you say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So were these soldiers -- and I guess several hundred metres from other military facilities such as B2 and B3. Now, when the soldiers that you heard going into rooms and when you heard small-arms fire after they went in there, were they going into military facilities to clear military facilities?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I would say no because just to the right from my apartment down, it was normal apartments, I mean people living there, and it was -- I located the sound from this kicking doors and so on from that building. And as far as I know, it was no military because I have seen people there before, I mean, civilian people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So the -- the kicking in doors and the small-arms fire was in one building in that area. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: It was a long building. I don't know how many apartments, but it was that building that I could hear, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, what happened or what did you hear when the HV went into the ARSK military facility in B1, their headquarters? What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I can't say anything about that because I can't sit in my apartment and see down to -- if you say the military, I didn't know it was the military house there. I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that -- your answer would, likewise, be the same in the facilities that we have designated as B8 or B2 or B3; is that right? You didn't hear anything when the HV went into those military facilities?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, on that same score, sir, as -- obviously you're not a military man, but you would expect an army going into particular areas to clear locations, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that's a normal practice in the military. Certainly, you were seconded to the military for a period of time. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the apartment buildings that you were -- that were being cleared, do you know whether or not there were any ARSK personnel living in those apartments?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No, I can't say that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I might have a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just to clarify, sir, when you say you can't say that, you don't if ARSK personnel were in those buildings, do you?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let me cover a couple of topics, sir, concerning the looting that you talked about on direct. And -- by the way, I mean, on the trucks that you told us that were going out with items in there, do you know how much of the stuff that was taken out there had been taken out of the military facilities like the Senjak barracks?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: If I say -- I don't know what kind of furniture they have in the barracks, but I can't imagine that they have chairs like this and -- I mean, not this, but, I mean, normal chairs where have you in your home. No. This was about the looting. I'm 100-percent sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, sir, I'm not questioning that you saw looting. I'm not questioning that at all. I'm not questioning that you saw them driving items out. I'm not saying that. I'm just saying that with some of the items that -- there were military facilities in Knin. You can't say from some of those items whether or not any of those items came from military facilities, can you?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. And when it came to that, that -- your observations that soldiers being drunk in town and acting, in your belief, without discipline, are you aware of anything that the commanding officers and the HV did to attempt to bring order and control over those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, when you walked out with -- and you were walking around with Norm Boucher. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you noted in your statement at -- and your statement, I'm talking about the 722, your 1998 statement at paragraph 29, that as of the morning of the 6th, the police station in Knin that you visited was up and running. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah, we saw policemen there, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And this was -- and you saw -- you went to the police station after you had come through the checkpoint where the soldiers, the military police, and the civilian police were located?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah, we went there -- from there, we went first to Norman's house where he was -- had his accommodation, and that house was completely blown up. And from there, we went to an apartment, and he said he will go inside to pick up something. I think that was one of the interpreters' apartment. And -- but when he came up there, it was military people inside this apartment, so he couldn't do this. And then we went up to the main road, and there you have the police station, the former milicija station. It was now a policija station. And there, one man came and said that, You are not allowed to be here, so he took us in his car and took us back to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And the person who took you back to the camp was a military policeman?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: He said he was the boss of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So at this police station on the morning of the 6th of August, was both military police --

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: It was not in the morning. It was -- because I came down to the camp, 7.00, and a couple of hours -- let's say 11.00, something -- 11, 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I know it's been a long time and these are estimates.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So around -- sometime midday on the 6th of August --

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- there was a police headquarters that was manned both by civilian police and by military police?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: As far as I can see, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Were you aware that on the 6th, the Croatian military, the HV turned the entire area over to the constitutional -- excuse me, the constitutional authority of the Republic of Croatia? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if I may, sir, in paragraph -- just talking about the looting just a bit. The -- in paragraph 20 -- excuse me, 34 of P722, this is where you said that the looting went on from approximately ten days from the 6th of August to the 16th of August. And I want to note for you an item that you addressed in your supplemental statement to the Prosecution, which the Prosecution did not ask you about, and that has to do with your statement at -- "The soldiers who were looting" -- this is what you told to the Prosecution. "The soldiers who were looting seemed to be acting individually. The looting didn't seem to be organised."

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And that was the statement that you gave to --

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: -- Ms. Gustafson?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, during this period of time, there was a -- you would agree as a police officer, there was a time needed to get the police department and the police up and running in the area. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I can only say what I saw this midday, that -- the policija was in that building, the old milicija building. I saw police officers there in their dark blue uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me -- are you familiar with some of the problems that they had to get up and running, the police department had to get up and running in the area?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I would say it was just to take over because it had been a policija station -- milicija station before, so just walk in and start it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let me -- if I can go --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I have a statement from a protected witness, Judge. If I could just go into private session briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, if we can just put D65 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Widen, this is the -- the item that you talked about on your direct examination, and this is the item that was -- excuse me. This is the item that was written on the day that you came to this location, isn't it, signed by you?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, when you went into this location, you note about midway down: "Because of the long time, it was impossible to see how the two men died."

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, this was written on the day of the event. Now, for the first time here, sir, you said that these men were shot?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah. Let's say it looks like that when we first came to the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In the statement that you did at the time, do you include anything that indicates that these people were shot, the statement that's on the screen, D65?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah. I don't -- can't remember if we --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just read it, sir.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: You don't say anything about them being shot, do you?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No, I'm not -- but let's say, this is something you -- in the situation like that and what I remember, it -- they didn't die a natural death.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, when you went with the Prosecution and they came to see you, and the date of this is -- pardon me a second. This is S -- 722. The 26th and the 27th of February, 2008, you discussed this particular report at paragraph 55 and paragraph 56, mainly paragraph 55. Now, in that particular paragraph in 2008, you don't say anything about these individuals being shot, do you?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let me turn your attention -- the two individuals that were killed were Milan Milivojevic and Ilija Milivojevic. Do you see that up there?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The two individuals? Let me turn your attention to D6.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'll put that on the screen, sir. Don't worry about it. I'll just put it on the screen. And in that item, first page is -- 6 and 7 is the name of Milan and -- 6 is Ilija and 7 is Milan. If we can go to the next page. Can we page up to this. I'm sorry. Let's go up to D7. Excuse me, D7. Thank you. Sir, D7 is the autopsy report for Ilija Milivojevic, and if you can read on the -- if you just look at the summary and the cause of death, and take your time with that. The medical examiner at the time was uncertain as to the cause of death, and there's nothing in the summary about any gunshot wound.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And let's go to D8, which is Milan Milivojevic. That, likewise, is nothing about any gunshot wounds in the autopsy, and there is no certainty on the part of the medical examiner about the time of death.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, you are mixing up comment and questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I apologise, Judge. I didn't mean to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Comment is about the absence of something. Of course we could have asked the witness, but of course, the Chamber can read it, as well, so there is no need to do that. And if there would be any comment, it would also be fair to say that, for example, and this will not -- well, no, I will leave my further comments for the time being. I might have some questions on the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, the autopsy that you just saw on both Ilija Milivojevic and Milan Milivojevic where they conclude that they cannot determine a cause of death, that's consistent with your written report on D65 where you also noted that it was impossible to see how the two men died. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So when you came in and earlier today said this was an exclusion that was your assumption; that wasn't your observation, was it?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No. I said it looked like, I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And when you say "look like it," that was based on your observation of gunshot wounds?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But you don't reflect that in any fashion in your report?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No, because in the -- what I'm saying to you now is the feeling I have and what -- and I, also, in my report said that we couldn't -- but if you ask me today, I would say they were shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let us take that the comment that you noted for the first time that this was an execution. If this was an execution, you don't know the circumstances of the execution, do you?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I mean, you noted that these bodies had been around for sometime?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah. It was very, very warm weather at that time, so let's say it won't take many days before the body start will rotting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, you don't know if these people were shot, assuming they were Serbs, if they were shot by other Serbs who were angry at them, do you?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I can't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And you don't know if they were shot by Croats coming back who were exacting revenge, can you?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I can't say that. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So it would be fair to say you don't know any of the circumstances involved?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No. I just told you what I -- got in mind when I saw this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Widen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can just have one moment, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Widen, thank you very much for your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kehoe. And, Mr. Kay --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]... remains as it was, that is ... Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will now be cross-examined, Mr. Widen, by Mr. Kuzmanovic who is counsel for Mr. Markac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Widen, who was your commander at UNCIVPOL? Who did you report to?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: In --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: In Knin.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I can't remember if it was -- Elleby, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Who did you work with when you went out on patrols in Knin?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Different people every time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Was there one particular -- person in particular that you went out on patrol with?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like you to refer to your statement, P722, paragraphs 37 and 38. If you have that statement in front of you, Mr. Widen, please pull it out so you can follow along.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: What paragraph you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: 37 and 38. 722 is the 2008 statement, and let me know if you've found the paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: On paragraph 38, you state that you patrolled through Knin anywhere from approximately 5 to 15 times after Operation Storm. Can you give us a range of dates after Operation Storm, from when to when that 5 to 15 times occurred?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Seven days, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And in paragraph 37, you stated that you never saw any burning during your few CIVPOL patrols in Knin but you saw burnt houses on the way to Benkovac, correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So in Knin itself, you never saw burning?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Paragraph 39 of that same statement, sir, the sentence begins: "During one of these patrols," and that's in Knin again, "a colleague of mine around I saw a mass grave near the cemetery." First, I'd like to ask you who the colleague was you were with?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I can't remember that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what gave you the conclusion that this was a mass grave?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: It was the size -- as I could see, it was 2 metre wide, about 2 metre deep, and around 30 metre long, and if -- what happened before, I thought this must be a prepared mass grave, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any -- there were no bodies that you saw, correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No -- No bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: No grave markers?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: No caskets?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Nothing more than the diggers were still in the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So you made an assumption that this was a mass grave?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 35, sir, you say: "When I was in Knin, I did not know any of the civilian or military authorities." Can you please give us a reference as to -- was this before or after Operation Storm that you did not know any of the civilian or military authorities?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I would say it was both when the Serbs were there or when the Croats there. I didn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't know who they were?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No. I didn't, and let's say my work was not to -- we have special guys who have the meeting with the chief of policija and so on, and I was not that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So it's fair to state that at least before and after Operation Storm your lack of familiarity of civilian or military authorities was the same?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly pause between questions and answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, you had already testified, sir, that on August 4th, 5th, and 6th, you were basically in your apartment?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: During the first three days of Operation Storm in Knin?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: From the 4th, at 5.00 when the shelling started, and then I stay inside the whole day and the whole night and until I think about 1800 on the -- on the 5th, it must be. On the 5th, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you were not picked up by any pre-Operation Storm UN patrol, correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: That's correct. I was the only one they left outside. I don't know why -- I have no idea why, but I think they forgot me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Was that because of poor organisation or for some other reason, or do you know?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I have another lady working in UN. She was living a house up -- very close to my house, and her, they pick up, so they must have been very close to me, and no, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So you were left behind?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, you decided to walk to the UN barracks?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: What was the -- what prompted you to do that?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I had to report that I was still alive, and before I left I asked those people to write their name, so I said when I'm coming to the UN, I will show the -- this report and you will tell the Croat soldiers when they're coming that you are still alive when I left on the 5th -- on the 6th, morning. So then I start walking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And how long did it take to you walk from your apartment to the UN barracks?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: 30, 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. And during that entire time, expect for one spot you did not see any dead bodies, correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And the dead bodies that you saw were two dead bodies, according to your statement, that were on a trailer?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: It was -- a tractor, and they were lying under the tractor. It was an old man and an old woman and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Lying underneath the tractor?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: But other than those two bodies -- I presume you don't have any idea how they died, Correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No, no. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Other than those two bodies that you saw, you did not see any other dead bodies in and around Knin from your walk to -- from your apartment to the UN barracks, correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: My statement's correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: That's correct, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe had discussed with you the supplemental information sheet, and he had asked you a question about that. I would ask the usher to please provide, if you don't have it, Mr. Widen, your supplemental information sheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we've had it put into e-court but it'S not yet up, so I have asked Mr. Monkhouse and the usher to provide the Court with copies, and of course, it's a proofing note from the Prosecution, so I did provide them with a copy as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, this proofing note, Mr. Widen, was signed by you on August 23rd, correct, of this year?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And one of the things Mr. Kehoe asked you about related to the issue of looting, and before we get to the -- the proofing note, I'd like you to refer, please, P721 which was your very first statement, Mr. Widen, of December 14th of 1995. And if you go to the very last page of that document -- actually, the very last sentence of the document. The very last sentence of your first statement says: "It was my impression that the looting was organised and authorised from higher up." And then in your supplemental note, on page 2, in the third -- fourth paragraph, it's quite a substantial -- it's actually completely the opposite that you state: "The soldiers who were looting seemed to be acting individually. The looting didn't seem to be organised."

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: On that, I can say that the feeling I have that time when I was there was that it was authorised from upper that you have the Knin city for yourself now for, let's say, five or ten days, and after that, we have to stop the looting, and this is -- many armies have done this before, so this is -- I think that was some kind of payment to the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: But your supplemental statement here says: "The looting didn't seem to be organised, and the soldiers who were looting seemed to be acting individually." Correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes. That what I remember now, but when I read what I was writing, 1995, it's more like that is the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: More like which is the truth?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: What I write in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: So what you're telling me is what you added in your supplemental statement is not the truth?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Let's say I can't remember exactly. If I go back to my mind, I can't say today what I have been written here. I mean, I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: By "written here," you mean in your very first statement?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. I mean, those are two substantially different versions of the events, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour. I'm almost done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: The -- page 5, Mr. Widen, of your very first statement, P721, the second-last sentence, it states: "I didn't personally witness any violence." And that is in Knin, correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And it -- was that throughout your whole time in Knin after Operation Storm that you did not witness any -- personally witness any violence?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: And by "violence," do you mean that that's a person against another person?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah. Beating up or shooting or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to ask you -- one other area I want to talk to you about, Mr. Widen. The procedure that UNCIVPOL has, for example, when you run across the site of a person or persons who have died or been killed, it's true, is it not, that UNCIVPOL upon coming on a scene like that would report that to the Croatian police, correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: You would not move the bodies?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: We never touched them. We just recognised the place, and then we contacted the policija, and they would come.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So if someone would move the bodies or try to take photographs or conduct their own investigation outside the Croatian civilian police, that would be a violation of UNCIVPOL procedure, would it not?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I was never with anybody doing that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: My question, however, was: If someone did do that from UNCIVPOL at any of these scenes were there was a murder, that would be a violation of UNCIVPOL procedure, would it not, to move a body from -- remove a body from a crime scene, potentially, correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: You are not allowed to do that because you had to go to the policija and tell them, and if we took photograph, I can't remember. But the investigation have to be done by the policija.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, what would you do after reporting something to the civilian police? What would your next step be, if anything? Would you follow up at all?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: We tried to, but it was very difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Can you give me an example of what you mean by you tried to but it was very difficult?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: If, for example, I asked the policeman coming to the scene what happened after, and he will never answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Any other example that you can give me?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Was it your general experience that when you called the Croatian civilian police to a crime scene that they would come and investigate the scene?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: They were coming, but about the investigation, I can't answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. They would come to the scene, and what happened after they came to the scene you don't know anything about?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. That's all the questions I have. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kuzmanovic. Ms. Gustafson, any need to put further questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: About five minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: You were asked at page 61 of today's transcript by Mr. Kehoe about the possibility that the Serbs may have fired back on the Croats during the shelling or at some point on the 4th and 5th, and I'd just like to ask you, you explain in your statement that the shelling ceased at 1.00 p.m.; you started to hear the sound of tanks and small-arms fire at 3.00 p.m. on the 5th. After the shelling ceased at 1.00 p.m., did you hear any other sounds that sounded to you like artillery fire?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: My second question is about the questions you were asked about problems the police may have had bringing law and order to the area, the police in Knin, and this was at page 68. Based on what you saw on the 6th/7th of August in Knin at the check-point at the policija station and around the town, did it appear to you that the civilian police in Knin were having problems getting up and running in the area?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No, I can't say, but as I -- on the 6th I saw two uniform police officer coming carrying video and a TV.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And what did that indicate to you?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: That they have picked it up somewhere, and I saw -- I said to Norman, Now our colleagues are looting, they -- them -- they also.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And page 5 of your 1995 statement, in the last paragraph you said: "According to what I witnessed, neither the civilian police nor the military police raised a finger to stop the looting of Knin."

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Did it appear to that you that this failure to stop the looting had to do with practical problems the police were having, or was it something else?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No. I don't know why they -- they let this go on, but after a couple of days, I can't say how many, the law and order came back, and it was okay again.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: This is the -- after the approximately 10-day period that you referred to in your statement?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And my last question is about burning. You were at asked at page 74 and you were referred to paragraph 37 of your 2008 statement. And that paragraph says: "During my few CIVPOL patrols from Knin, I never saw any burning, but I saw burnt houses on the way to Benkovac."

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Are those patrols that you undertook in the area from Knin to the outside of Knin, or are you talking about patrols in Knin in that paragraph, or do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No -- sometimes we went outside Knin, and I can't remember why we were at that place, but it was, as I remember, two or three houses burnt down, and how that happened, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: When you were asked about this paragraph, you agreed that you didn't see any burning in Knin, but at page 3 of your 1995 statement you describe the first patrol you took on the 6th, and you say: "A block of flats and an office block were on fire, but I don't know whether this was as a result of a shell or arson." Is that correct? Do you recall seeing fire in Knin on the 6th --

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Now -- now when you say it, I remember that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Those are my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can I just ask one follow-up question, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but let's -- I'm looking at the clock. Let me just confer with my colleagues for a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since there are some questions from the Bench, as well, we consider it wiser to take the break now for 20 minutes. Then I will allow you to put one or more questions, and then the Bench will have some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have a break until ten minutes past 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have one more question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, one more question. Further cross-examination by Mr. Kehoe:

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Mr. Widen, just to follow up on Ms. Gustafson' question to you -- statement to you about in your statement, neither the civil police or military police raised a finger to stop the looting. I mean, you have no knowledge of the internal functioning of the military police or the civilian police, do you?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: You mean in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: In Croatia.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kehoe. Judge Kinis has one or more questions for you, one or more. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: I would like to ask you a question regarding your statement, 2008, paragraph 89. When you mentioned that you find this mass -- the preparation of this mass grave, and finally you mentioned whether you or your colleague reported about this, you didn't recall, but that would have been the normal practice. What -- could you please explain? What do you mean about --

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I can't explain that. I didn't make a report on it, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: No, no, but this last sentence, that would be -- would have been the normal practice.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: To do so, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: To report?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: Oh. And if it would -- was not reported, it was something out of normal practice?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: It was, and the only explanation I have is that I thought my colleague would make the report. That's the only --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: Okay. And you mentioned there in Location L in this map provided by Prosecutor to us, to Chamber, as well, that there is this location of this mass grave.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: Yes. Was -- and as far as I understood -- or maybe it is not correct; maybe you can clarify this issue. Where this mass grave was prepared, inside cemetery territory or outside cemetery?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: Outside.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes. And if you stand in front, it was to the left of the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KINIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have a few questions for you, as well, Mr. Widen. You told us that you saw Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you also told us that you recognised him by the hat he was wearing.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us, was it only by the hat --

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that you recognised him or were there any other features which made you recognise him?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I recognised him from pictures, and it was him. I'm 100-percent sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the hat was in addition to --

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: It was -- any picture I have seen of Mr. Mladic is when he have this hat on. It was a very special one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, of course, I do not know whether such a hat is specific for a man in his position, yes or no. So I do understand that you recognised him by the picture, but by the hat on the pictures or the face on the pictures?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: The face and the hat, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The face and the hat. Thank you for that answer.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you said that you have seen Mr. Tudjman arriving in a helicopter.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give us a bit more details about what you observed.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: It was, let's say, a lot of celebration, and all of us know that Mr. Tudjman will come by the helicopter, and I saw the helicopter, so I didn't see Mr. Tudjman himself because that was up at the castle, and you were not allowed to go up there. So I was very close to this, and I saw the helicopter so it came, and they told me that Mr. Tudjman was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So what you actually observed and heard is stories about Mr. Tudjman --

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yeah, and that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that he would arrive in a helicopter, and you saw a helicopter?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Landing --

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: At the castle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- At the castle. Thank you for that answer. Now, you told us about the objects that were, as you told us, looted, and you talked about electronics.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you intend to refer us to just electronics or any electrical equipment?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: What I called electronic is TV and the videos, and that what I saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No washing machines, no hair dryers, no --

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Then you -- quite a lot of questions were put to you about individual looting and the looting not being organised or giving the impression to be organised. Now, I would like not to hear about your impressions, but I would like to know exactly on what facts you came to the conclusions at various moments. And let me take you to part of your testimony. You said you had seen trucks.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fully loaded.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: With objects, one person in the front, one or two others --

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- at the back. Now, is that for you, if it would be a military vehicle, and I think you -- you also told us about military vehicles, would that be a fact which you would be consider in favour of organised looting or in favour of individual looting or looting committed by individuals?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: One way you must say it was organised, if you think back, because those vehicles, one soldier couldn't take one vehicle and start looting himself, so what I figure out that was the trucks were leaving Knin, and I think they were coming back when they have unloaded the trucks and taking more goods.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, just on the basis of your testimony that one driver, two or three at the back, more?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I can't say, but I saw soldier in the back of the trucks, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, to the extent you remember, would there have been televisions for more than the two, three, or four? Would that be eight televisions or ten, or would it be limited to the number of persons that accompanied the transport?

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: I would say it's between 50 and 100 trucks I saw leaving Knin, between that during those days, but I can't say how many, but at least 50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but that's the number of trucks.

utterances.speaker: ERIK LENNART WIDEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
